text: A student reads a blog about nuclear power.
In 2017, 10.5% of the world’s electricity was generated from 454 nuclear
power stations. Nuclear power produces a lot of energy from a small mass
Nuclear power stations use heat to produce steam to turn turbines, which
drive generators. The heat comes from nuclear fission. Nuclear fission splits
the nuclei of uranium atoms to release large amounts of energy.
In 2017, 38% of the world’s uranium production came from Kazakhstan.
This was 23 300 tonnes of uranium. Canada produced 13 100 tonnes, which
was 22%, and Australia’s production was 5900 tonnes, which was 10%.
